checks_performed: Read only the specified source input and draft; used no web resources or other source files.
Independently re-derived the finite-field connection sets, conference-matrix identity, Fourier formulation, and Jacobi-sum eigenvalue formula, including exceptional and trivial-character cases.
Checked the theta product, monotonicity, additivity, Paley self-complementarity, spectral bound, induced-subgraph bound, and all asymptotic deductions under the stated theta convention.

Created and ran an exact-arithmetic checker using rational arithmetic and Q(√2). It verifies matching Fourier primal/dual certificates for p=5,13,17 and exhaustively checks every p=17 perfect matching and vertex permutation.

claims.claim: Writing Q for the nonzero squares and K_p=complement(H_p), both H_p and K_p are Cayley graphs on the multiplicative group Q. Their connection sets S and T have sizes (p−5)/4 and (p−1)/4, respectively.
claims.evidence: For x,y∈Q, χ(x−y)=χ(x/y−1), so adjacency depends only on the multiplicative ratio. Because χ(−1)=1, both connection sets are inverse-closed. Moreover, Σ_{q∈Q}χ(q−1)=½(Σ_{x≠0}χ(x−1)+Σ_xχ(x(x−1)))=½(−1−1)=−1. Together with |S|+|T|=|Q|−1=(p−3)/2, this gives |S|=(p−5)/4 and |T|=(p−1)/4.
claims.search_method: Direct quadratic-character calculation valid for every prime p≡1 mod 4.

claims.claim: The localized Paley sign matrix B has operator norm at most √p, by an exact conference-matrix identity.
claims.evidence: For C_{xy}=χ(x−y) on F_p, exact character correlation gives C²=pI−J. Ordering F_p as {0}, Q, and {ν/q:q∈Q} for a nonsquare ν yields Q-blocks B and D with B²+D²=pI−2J. Hence ||Bv||²=p||v||²−2(1ᵀv)²−||Dv||²≤p||v||² for every real v.
claims.search_method: Exact block-matrix derivation from the quadratic-character correlation identity.

claims.claim: θ(K_p) is exactly an explicit finite Fourier linear program, or equivalently a nonnegative-vector problem for a half-dimensional Fourier projection.
claims.evidence: Averaging a feasible theta matrix over multiplicative translations of Q gives X_{xy}=f(x⁻¹y)/n, with f(1)=1, f zero on the K_p connection set T, inverse symmetry, and nonnegative Fourier coefficients; these conditions are also sufficient. The objective is Σ_q f(q). With y_ψ=f̂(ψ)/n, the constraints become y≥0, Σy=1, and θ(K_p)=n y_triv. Support of f on D={1}∪S is exactly P_Dy=y, where P_D is the Fourier-conjugate of coordinate projection onto D and has rank |D|=n/2. Conjugate character coordinates may be identified, giving the real formulation.
claims.search_method: Direct averaging of the SDP followed by finite abelian Fourier diagonalization.

claims.claim: Every nontrivial Fourier eigenvalue of B is the real part of a Jacobi sum of modulus √p.
claims.evidence: For nontrivial ψ on Q and either extension A to F_p*, neither A nor Aχ is trivial. The eigenvalue is R_ψ=½(J(A,χ)+J(Aχ,χ)). Standard Gauss-sum identities apply without an exceptional-character case and give |J(A,χ)|=|J(Aχ,χ)|=√p and J(A,χ)J(Aχ,χ)=G(χ)²=p because p≡1 mod 4. Thus the two Jacobi sums are conjugates and R_ψ=Re J(A,χ).
claims.search_method: Exact multiplicative-character and Gauss-sum derivation, with all possible extensions checked.

claims.claim: For every vertex-transitive graph G on n vertices, θ(G)θ(complement(G))=n.
claims.evidence: The SDP dual tI+Z−J⪰0 yields the general product lower bound. For the reverse direction, average an optimal primal matrix X over a transitive automorphism group. Then diag X=1/n and X1=(θ(G)/n)1. Consequently (n²/θ(G))X−J is positive semidefinite and is a dual certificate for complement(G) with value n/θ(G), proving equality.
claims.search_method: Primal-dual proof under the exact SDP convention in the target.

claims.claim: Theta is monotone under taking induced subgraphs.
claims.evidence: Any feasible matrix for an induced subgraph extends by zero rows and columns to a feasible matrix for the original graph, preserving trace, positive semidefiniteness, edge zeros, and objective value.
claims.search_method: Direct feasible-solution extension in the defining SDP.

claims.claim: Theta is additive on disjoint unions: θ(G⊔L)=θ(G)+θ(L).
claims.evidence: In Gram form, optimizers for the components can be rotated so their vector sums align and scaled with trace shares proportional to their theta values, attaining θ(G)+θ(L). Conversely, if the component trace shares are a,b, their vector-sum norms are at most √(aθ(G)) and √(bθ(L)); Cauchy–Schwarz then bounds the union objective by (a+b)(θ(G)+θ(L))=θ(G)+θ(L).

claims.claim: The full Paley graph P_p satisfies θ(P_p)=√p.
claims.evidence: Translations make P_p vertex-transitive, while multiplication by a nonsquare is an isomorphism from P_p to its complement. Applying the verified vertex-transitive product identity gives θ(P_p)²=p, and theta is positive.
claims.search_method: Graph automorphisms plus the vertex-transitive theta product identity.

claims.evidence: Multiplication by a nonsquare identifies K_p with the Paley graph induced on the nonsquares N. Vertex 0 has no Paley neighbor in N, so P_p[{0}∪N] is K_p disjoint union an isolated vertex. Induced-subgraph monotonicity and additivity therefore give 1+θ(K_p)≤θ(P_p)=√p.
claims.search_method: Explicit induced-subgraph embedding followed by theta monotonicity and additivity.

claims.evidence: H_p is d=(p−5)/4 regular on n=(p−1)/2 vertices. On 1⊥ its adjacency eigenvalues are (R_ψ−1)/2, so its least eigenvalue τ satisfies τ≥−(√p+1)/2. The exact dual certificate tI+cA−J with c=n/(d−τ) and t=−nτ/(d−τ) gives θ(H_p)≤−nτ/(d−τ), which is at most (√p+1)²/(√p+3). The exceptional case p=5 is an empty two-vertex graph and both sides equal 2.
claims.search_method: Spectral SDP-dual certificate, with p=5 checked separately.

claims.evidence: The upper bound is claim 8. Since H_p is a Cayley graph and hence vertex-transitive, θ(H_p)θ(K_p)=n. Dividing n=(p−1)/2 by the verified upper bound (√p+1)²/(√p+3) for θ(H_p) yields exactly the stated lower bound.
claims.search_method: Exact algebraic combination of the complementary product identity and preceding bounds.

claims.claim: The proven bounds imply 1/√2≤liminf θ(K_p)/√(p/2)≤limsup θ(K_p)/√(p/2)≤√2, and isolate the unresolved step as asymptotic balance of the complementary theta numbers.
claims.evidence: After division by √(p/2), the lower and upper bounds tend respectively to 1/√2 and √2. Since θ(H_p)θ(K_p)=(p−1)/2, the requested limit is equivalent to both theta numbers being asymptotic to √((p−1)/2), i.e. to their asymptotic balance. None of the established bounds proves that balance.
claims.search_method: Exact normalization of the two-sided bounds and use of the complementary product identity.

claims.claim: The exact small-prime values are θ(K_5)=1, θ(K_13)=2, θ(K_17)=8−4√2; correspondingly θ(H_5)=2, θ(H_13)=3, and θ(H_17)=2+√2.
claims.evidence: The exact checker passed. For p=13, the Fourier primal a=1/2 attains 2 and the l=3 inequality 1−2a≥0 proves optimality. For p=17, a=2−√2 and b=3−2√2 are Fourier-feasible and attain 8−4√2; the positive combination (4−2√2) times the l=3 inequality plus (3−2√2) times the l=4 inequality proves the matching upper bound. The p=5 graphs are respectively K_2 and the empty two-vertex graph. Complementary values follow exactly from the product identity.
claims.search_method: Executed symbolic primal/dual Fourier certificates using Fraction arithmetic and an exact Q(√2) implementation; no floating-point decisions.
claims.witness: p=13 certificate a=1/2; p=17 certificate a=2−√2, b=3−2√2 with dual weights 4−2√2 and 3−2√2.

claims.claim: A tempting exact explanation—K_p being a relabelled copy of H_p with one perfect matching added—is already false for p=17.
claims.evidence: The checker constructs H_17=Cay(Z/8Z,{±1,4}) and K_17=Cay(Z/8Z,{±2,±3}) directly from quadratic residues modulo 17. Because their degrees are 3 and 4, any proposed extension must arise by deleting a perfect matching from K_17. All 14 perfect matchings were enumerated, and every resulting graph was compared with H_17 over all 8! vertex bijections; none is isomorphic. Independently, H_17 has no triangles and four induced 4-cycles, whereas twelve deletions retain triangles and the two triangle-free deletions have six induced 4-cycles.
claims.search_method: Exact exhaustive enumeration of all perfect matchings and all graph relabellings on eight vertices.
claims.witness: p=17: none of the 14 perfect-matching deletions from K_17 is isomorphic to H_17.

target_evidence: The exact target requires proving that θ(complement(H_p))/√(p/2) tends to 1, or proving that the limit is not 1. The draft explicitly states that it proves neither. Its verified results give only asymptotic constants between 1/√2 and √2 and an equivalent balance formulation, so they constitute material but incomplete progress. The final writeup does not claim otherwise, and its claimed_resolution of PARTIAL is therefore accurate.
